method.lean: fixed-weight blend of the district's own House general result (0.20), the state's midterm statewide ballot (0.20: governor / attorney general / secretary of state / state treasurer, plus state-leg chamber totals over contested state-leg districts) and its pooled U.S. Senate races (0.20) — the unified lean scheme minus the presidential component — each as Democratic two-party share minus the same race's national share; weights renormalised over the sources present (≈ 1/3 each when all three are up, 50/50 house + statewide when no Senate race is on the ballot) — districts without a usable House race fall back to the statewide blend (statewide_baseline)

components.house: the district's own U.S. House general result from data/house/house_results_{year}.csv; winner votes missing in the article are reconstructed from percentage x district turnout; one-sided races dropped as uninformative
components.senate: U.S. Senate general races (regular + special) from data/senate/senate_general_results_{year}.csv
components.statewide: governor / attorney general / secretary of state / state treasurer races from data/statewide/statewide_general_results_{year}.csv
components.state-leg: state senate + state house votes aggregated to statewide chamber totals from data/state_senate/ and data/state_house/ (state-leg districts cannot be mapped to congressional districts, so they enter only as chamber sums); walkover state-leg districts (a major party polled no votes) are dropped before the aggregation

method.two_party: party lines summed as reported: fusion lines (Working Families, Conservative, Independence, ...) count on their own line party and land in other_votes, excluded from the two-party baseline; Total rows excluded; write-ins = other
method.race_exclusion: races where a major party polled zero votes (top-two / top-four matchups such as CA 2016 or AK 2022 senate) are dropped as uninformative before blending
method.national_baseline: each component's national baseline is that component summed over all district-map states with data; territories (PR, GU, MP, ...) excluded
caveats: the statewide components (senate / statewide executive / state-leg) carry no district detail, so districts without a usable House race share the state's blended baseline

the statewide blend follows each state's actual ballot (not every state has a senate race up; AG appears from 2018, SoS/treasurer from 2022), so national baselines are not directly comparable across years
state-leg chamber totals cover the states whose legislative races the source parses (11-24 states before 2016, 39-41 from 2020) and count contested districts only
the 2020s crosswalk snapshot includes the 2024 AL/GA/LA/NY/NC court redraws, while the 2022 midterms voted on the pre-redraw lines
DC has no senate race and no statewide-executive rows in the source tables, so DC-AL leans on its House delegate race alone where one is parsed
